facts.fact: NMC Graduate Medical Education Regulations 2023, reg. 11(b): a candidate may take NEET-UG only after passing 10+2 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English.

NMC GMER 2023, reg. 11(a): the candidate must have completed 17 years on or before 31 January (as printed in the gazette text) of the year of appearing in NEET-UG; the year's Information Bulletin governs the exact date and any upper-age rule (not confirmed).

NMC GMER 2023, reg. 9: no student may pursue graduate medical education in India (or abroad, if returning to practise in India) without scoring the minimum eligible score in NEET-UG; UGMEB announces the eligible list by notification. The regulation text gives no percentile or PCB-marks figure.
NMC GMER 2023, reg. 10: ties in NEET-UG marks are broken by marks in Physics, then Chemistry, then Biology; if still tied, a computer draw with no human intervention.

NMC GMER 2023, reg. 12-15: there is common counselling for all medical institutions in India based on the NEET-UG merit list, on the seat matrix provided by NMC; the Government of India notifies the agency conducting counselling.
NEET (UG) 2026 was first held on 3 May 2026; a re-examination was held on 21 June 2026, 2:00 PM to 5:15 PM including 15 minutes of formalities (NTA FAQ); result declared 16 July 2026 (NTA notice).
NTA public notice of 20 July 2026 states the NEET (UG) 2026 result was declared on 16 July 2026, after the 21 June 2026 re-examination.

NTA FAQ: the medium of examination chosen in the application form is final and cannot be changed; the Information Bulletin (Chapter 4, para 6(ix)) lists medium options by State/location; re-exam centres could differ from the first one.
NTA said the NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination on 21 June 2026 was administered in 13 languages including Hindi and English, for over 20 lakh candidates at 5,440 centres in India and 14 abroad.

NTA public notice of 20 July 2026 refers to an OMR answer sheet with 180 answer bubbles (i.e. 180 questions); it warns that fabricated or AI-altered OMR sheets or score cards are an offence under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
The last date for the NEET (UG) 2026 online application was extended to 11 March 2026 (9 PM; fee payment up to 11:50 PM).

DCI BDS Course Regulations 2007 (as amended, text on the DCI site): 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English individually passed, and at least 50% marks in PCB taken together (40% for SC/ST/OBC; 45% for candidates with locomotory disability of lower limbs).

DCI BDS regulations: age 17 on or before 31 December of the admission year; NEET percentile 50th (General), 40th (SC/ST/OBC), 45th (locomotory disability), which the Central Government may lower for a year. These are 2007-era regulations; confirm in the current NEET bulletin.

VCI bulletin 2026-27: admission to the 15% all-India quota BVSc & AH seats is through the NEET (UG) 2026 merit list; 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English (core), minimum 50% aggregate in these subjects (47.5% for SC/ST/other special categories); minimum age 17 on 31 December 2026; 858 seats in the 15% quota.
VCI 15% quota reservation: SC 15%, ST 7.5%, EWS 10%, OBC-NCL 27%, PwD 5% horizontal.

Indian Nursing Council eligibility page: B.Sc Nursing needs 10+2 Science (PCB) and English (core or elective) with 45% aggregate; minimum age 17 on 31 December of the admission year; medically fit. The page gives no category-wise relaxation for B.Sc (N).

INC draft (to be gazetted) 2022 corrigendum: entrance qualifying percentile General 50th, SC/ST/OBC 40th, General-PwD 45th, SC/ST/OBC-PwD 40th; for SC/ST/OBC 40% in Physics, Chemistry, Biology and a pass in English. Whether it is in force is not confirmed; states and universities set their own admission route.

ICAR undergraduate admission 2026-27 is through CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 (NTA); qualifying: 10+2 with at least three subjects out of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture; 50% aggregate (General, OBC-NCL, UPS, EWS) and 40% (SC, ST, Third Gender, PwBD); minimum age 16 on 31.08.2026; universities add their own subject combinations and age limits.
CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2026-27 lists Physics (042), Chemistry (043) and Biology (044) each as 070 theory + 030 practical.
Biology (044) 2026-27 Class XII: theory 70 marks in 3 hours; practical 30 marks in 3 hours.

Class XII Biology 2026-27 theory units: VI Reproduction 16, VII Genetics and Evolution 20, VIII Biology and Human Welfare 12, IX Biotechnology and its Applications 12, X Ecology and Environment 10 (total 70).
Biology practical (30): major experiment 5, minor experiment 4, slide preparation 5, spotting 7, record + viva 4, investigatory project + record + viva 5.

Environmental Issues (air and water pollution, solid wastes, agro-chemicals, radioactive wastes, greenhouse effect, ozone depletion, deforestation) stays in the 2026-27 syllabus but is assessed only formatively, not in summative assessment.
Class XII Physics 2026-27: theory 70 marks in 3 hours (9 units, 14 chapters), practical 30 marks in 3 hours.

Class XII Chemistry 2026-27: theory 70 marks in 3 hours (10 chapters: Solutions 7, Electrochemistry 9, Chemical Kinetics 7, d- and f-Block 7, Coordination Compounds 7, Haloalkanes 6, Alcohols-Phenols-Ethers 6, Aldehydes-Ketones-Acids 8, Amines 6, Biomolecules 7); practical 30 marks (volumetric analysis 8, salt analysis 8, content-based experiment 6, project 4, record and viva 4).

CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2026-27: the Board conducts Annual examinations for Class XII covering the entire Class XII syllabus; 9-point grading in each elective subject. No second Board exam for Class XII is described in this document.
The Physics curriculum 2026-27 notes that content shown as excluded in the NCERT textbooks for 2026-27 is not to be tested.
The NEET (UG) 2026 syllabus was issued through an NTA notice dated 8 January 2026 (scanned PDF, text not machine-readable, contents not confirmed).

routes.name: NEET (UG) for MBBS: Class 12 marks in PCB
routes.note: The NMC regulations confirm the subjects (Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Biotechnology, and English) but give no percentage. The 50 / 40 / 45 figures here are the DCI rule for BDS, used as a guide: the NEET bulletin could not be read. Confirm in the NEET (UG) information bulletin.

routes.name: BDS: Class 12 marks in PCB
routes.confidence: official page (DCI regulations, 2007 text as amended)
routes.note: The third figure (45%) is for a lower-limb locomotory disability, not every benchmark disability. Confirm in the current NEET bulletin and DCI notices.

routes.name: BVSc & AH, 15% all-India quota (via NEET)
routes.note: Aggregate of English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology: 50%, and 47.5% for SC/ST and other special categories. No separate figure for the third category was found, so the General figure is used.

routes.name: B.Sc Nursing: PCB and English
routes.confidence: official page (INC), with one part not confirmed
routes.note: The INC page says 45% aggregate and states no category relaxation. A draft 2022 INC corrigendum gives 40% for SC/ST/OBC but is not confirmed in force, so the reserved category shows Check between 40% and 45%. The admission route is set by your state or university.

routes.name: B.Sc Agriculture (ICAR, via CUET UG 2026)
routes.note: Counted over all Class 12 subjects, not PCB only; at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture. 50% General, OBC-NCL and EWS; 40% SC, ST and PwBD. Universities add their own conditions.

notes: BAMS / BUMS / BSMS, BHMS and B.Pharm are not in the calculator: their official pages could not be read (blocked or not connecting), so no Class 12 percentage could be confirmed for them. Check the notice of the council or your state.
